requires: The source explicit n+2-state family, additive rank-one control definitions, identification task, uniform error criterion, allowed adaptive policies and supplied fast fixed-mode relaxation. Full transition/task/protocol definitions are in the unacquired report; they are not reconstructed from a numerical headline.
Total available actuation amplitude B is constrained and concurrent fractional controls obey the same declared model. Background reset and channels are supplied resources.
provides: A SEPARATE explicit n+2-state family has additive rank-one controls, known fast fixed-mode relaxation and no exponentially small positive rates. Under total actuation amplitude B, acquisition-time lower bound is exponential in order n/(B+2); a fractional concurrent-control protocol matches the order, with B=Theta(n/log n) threshold for polynomial-time identification IN THAT FAMILY. At n64,budget1 requires at least20588177 native time units for uniform95% identification; all64 controls concurrently available protocol uses305.0932 and96 snapshots and was executed. Channel availability/background reset are supplied; source-state locality is not spatial many-body locality.
assumptions: This is a family-specific matching-order construction, not a universal lower bound for boundary control or the exclusion example. No exponentially small positive rates are required in the declared family.
Source-state locality does not imply spatial many-body locality. General partial-observation combination-lock hardness is prior machinery.
The all64-control protocol was executed; the budget-one value is a stated uniform-identification lower bound. These are different evidence roles.
costs: Actuation amplitude, simultaneous channel availability, supplied reset, native acquisition time and snapshots. More hardware/control capacity is not a free operation.
